title: Combined product

```{bash}
eval "$(pixi shell-hook)"
```

```{bash}
SOFTWARE_ROOT=../../lstm-wp3-products/products/ua
DOCKER_IMAGE_ID=hw-uacomb:1
OUTPUT_PATH="$(pwd)/outputs/urban_atlas"
ls -ltrAh --color=never "$SOFTWARE_ROOT"
```

## Conformance Class "Application"


### Requirement 1: req/app/cmd-line & Requirement 2: req/app/container

**req/app/cmd-line**

> The Application SHALL be a non-interactive executable as a command-line application.


**req/app/container**

> The environment, libraries, binaries, executable and configuration files necessary to execute the Application SHALL be bundled in a container image.

Requirement `req/app/cmd-line` can be shown by running an EOAP which includes a CommandLineTool with a docker requirement. To execute via CWL, the application must be executable on the command line (this is the mechanism that CWL uses) and a DockerRequirement makes sure this execution happens as a container. By running the application, we can see that no interactive input is required.

By running the command line using the container image, we show that everything required is avaiable in a container image.

The software product contains a run script to execute docker directly:

```{bash}
cat "$SOFTWARE_ROOT"/run.sh
```

```{bash}
mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_PATH"
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" --workdir=/home/mambauser/wd -v $SOFTWARE_ROOT/data:/home/mambauser/data -v $SOFTWARE_ROOT/inputs:/home/mambauser/wd/inputs -v "$OUTPUT_PATH":/home/mambauser/wd $DOCKER_IMAGE_ID || FAIL_REQ_1_2=1
ls -ltrAh --color=never $OUTPUT_PATH
```

### Requirement 3: req/app/registry

**req/app/registry**

> The Application container image SHALL be accessible in a container registry.

We can verify that the docker image used above is the same as specified in the CWL CommandLineTool:

```{bash}
echo "Docker image ID: $DOCKER_IMAGE_ID"
yq -M '."$graph"[1].requirements' "$SOFTWARE_ROOT/app/eoap.cwl"
yq -M '."$graph"[1].requirements.DockerRequirement.dockerPull' "$SOFTWARE_ROOT/app/eoap.cwl"
```

And that this docker image is available in a registry :

```{bash}
docker manifest inspect $DOCKER_IMAGE_ID || FAIL_REQ_3=1 | head -n 20
```

### Requirement 4: req/app/stac-input

**req/app/stac-input**

> An Application input argument that requires staged EO product files SHALL be defined as an argument that points to a folder where a STAC Catalog, named catalog.json, contains a list of one or more STAC Items and associated STAC Assets referencing the files.

We can inspect the CWL document to verify that there are inputs with the `Directory` type:

```{bash}
yq -M -e '(."$graph"[] | select(.class == "Workflow")).inputs[] | select(.type == "Directory")' $SOFTWARE_ROOT/app/eoap.cwl || FAIL_REQ_4=1
```

And inspect the input directories we will later provide to the process.

<!-- TODO inputs will be placed somewhere else than the software root -->
```{bash}
ls -ltrAh --color=never $SOFTWARE_ROOT/inputs/urban_atlas
```

```{bash}
ls -ltrAh --color=never $SOFTWARE_ROOT/inputs/material_labels
```

```{bash}
ls -ltrAh --color=never $SOFTWARE_ROOT/inputs/hcspots
```

```{bash}
cat $SOFTWARE_ROOT/inputs/urban_atlas/catalog.json
```

### Requirement 5: req/app/stac-out

**req/app/stac-out**

> An Application that creates EO product files to be stage-out SHALL generate a valid STAC Catalog, named catalog.json, and include the STAC Item(s) and corresponding STAC Assets pointing to the results of the processing.

We can inspect the output of the application that we ran with docker above.

```{bash}
ls -ltrAh --color=never "$OUTPUT_PATH"
```

With stac-validator, we verify that the output catalog and all referenced items are valid:

```{bash}
stac-validator validate --recursive $OUTPUT_PATH/catalog.json | cat || FAIL_REQ_5=1
```


### Requirement 6: rec/app/stac-out-metadata

> The STAC Catalog created by the Application SHALL include metadata elements for each STAC Item with at least their spatial (geometry, box) and temporal (datetime) properties.


## Conformance Class "Application Package"

### Requirement 7: req/app-pck/cwl

> The Application Package SHALL be a valid CWL document with a “Workflow” class and one or more “CommandLineTool” classes.


```{bash}
cwltool --disable-color --validate ../../lstm-wp3-products/products/ua/app/eoap.cwl | cat
```

- Warning is okay, there is no "main" because platforms may manage their main on their own accord

## Setup is valid (Directory + STAC)

This is still ua

```{bash}
tree -n ../../lstm-wp3-products/products/ua/inputs
```

## Can run to produce output

```{bash}
cwltool --disable-color --outdir ../cwlruns/combined ../../lstm-wp3-products/products/ua/app/eoap.cwl#heatwise_combined --urban_atlas ../../lstm-wp3-products/products/ua/inputs/urban_atlas --hcspots  ../../lstm-wp3-products/products/ua/inputs/hcspots --material_labels ../../lstm-wp3-products/products/ua/inputs/material_labels | cat
```

## output contains required fields

### Requirement 6: STAC Metadata (rec/app/stac-out-metadata)

> The STAC Catalog created by the Application SHALL include metadata elements for each STAC Item with at least their spatial (geometry, box) and temporal (datetime) properties.

Test validity
```{bash}
jq -M 'has("geometry") and has("bbox") and has("properties") and (.properties | has("datetime"))' cwlruns/combined/zeb8irli/datasets_saved/urban_atlas_with_hotspots.json || :
```

Show

```{bash}
jq -M '{name: .bbox, properties: .properties}' cwlruns/combined/zeb8irli/datasets_saved/urban_atlas_with_hotspots.json | cat

```

```{bash}
jq -M '{geometry: .geometry}' cwlruns/combined/zeb8irli/datasets_saved/urban_atlas_with_hotspots.json | head -n 20
```


### Report

```{bash}
if [[ -z "$FAIL_REQ_1_2" ]] then echo "req/app/cmd-line & req/app/container"; fi
if [[ -z "$FAIL_REQ_3" ]] then echo "req/app/registry"; fi
if [[ -z "$FAIL_REQ_4" ]] then echo "req/app/stac-input"; fi
if [[ -z "$FAIL_REQ_5" ]] then echo "req/app/stac-out"; fi
```
